hints.text: Dividing by ten makes a number ten times smaller. What happens to each digit's place when that happens?
Each digit of $6{,}000$ slides one place to the right, so the $6$ moves from the thousands place to the hundreds place.
A $6$ in the hundreds place is $600$, so $6{,}000 \div 10 = 600$.

explanation: Dividing by $10$ makes a number ten times smaller, which moves every digit one place to the right.
In $6{,}000$ the $6$ is in the thousands place, so after dividing it lands in the hundreds place.
That gives $6{,}000 \div 10 = 600$, and the check $600 \times 10 = 6{,}000$ agrees.
